INDEPENDENT THERMAL WINDOW ATTACK
Author-role: thermal_blind. Frozen before exposure to any other worker's thermal argument.
UTC freeze: 2026-10-08 08:06 (the timestamp is approximate; see FREEZE_MANIFEST.json).

STATUS AND EXACT SCOPE
The independent derivation proves a strictly positive asymptotic trace-distance lower bound from the set of ALL fully separable N-qubit states for 0<c<c_*, where c_* is the unique solution m(c_*)=1/2. Numerically c_*=0.3281137030571. The number is a numerical diagnostic; the threshold is defined exactly by its integral. This is a sufficient robust-entanglement region, not a proved separability transition. No exact limiting distance or separable approximation for c>=c_* has been obtained. The proof of the uniform fully separable witness bound below is the main result.

No thermal_window report or repository thermal proof argument was read. The supplied stationary block formula and BRIEF.txt were the only repository inputs. Primary spin-squeezing literature was checked after the witness mechanism had been derived. This report makes no novelty or priority claim.

PINNED INPUT
N spin-1/2 particles. J_a=(1/2)sum_i sigma_a^(i), J^2=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2. Initial state I/2^N. The supplied stationary state for (nu+1)D[J_-]+nu D[J_+] is
 rho_N = direct_sum_j w_Nj tau_j,beta tensor I_mult/mult,
 w_Nj = (2j+1) mult_Nj / 2^N,
 tau_j,beta = exp(-beta J_z)/Z_j,
 beta_N = log(1+1/(c sqrt(N))), c>0 fixed.
The direct-sum weights preserve exactly Tr rho_N J^2=3N/4.
The target distance is d_N(c)=inf_{sigma in fullSEP} (1/2)||rho_N-sigma||_1.

THEOREM 1: EXACT ASYMPTOTIC FULLSEP HEAT-EFFECT BOUND
For each t>0 and each fixed vector v in R^3, define
 B_N(v) = sum_a (J_a/sqrt(N)-v_a)^2,
 W_N(t,v) = exp[-t B_N(v)].
Then 0<=W_N<=I and
 lim_{N->infinity} sup_{sigma in fullSEP} Tr sigma W_N(t,v)
       = 1/(1+t/2).
The supremum allows arbitrary inhomogeneous product states and arbitrary mixtures, without permutation invariance or an IID assumption.

Proof, reduction to product arrays.
W_N is a linear objective, and fullSEP is the convex hull of pure product states. It is enough to bound any sequence pi_N=product_i rho_Ni, allowing mixed factors as well. Write r_Ni for the local Bloch vectors, |r_Ni|<=1, and put
 u_N = (1/(2sqrt(N))) sum_i r_Ni,
 Q_N = (1/N) sum_i r_Ni r_Ni^T,
 Sigma_N = (I-Q_N)/4.
